title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 90 (Register of significant beneficial owners)

content.overview: Section 90 requires declaration and a register of significant beneficial owners, and empowers the company and the Tribunal to act on non-disclosure.
content.glance: Section 90 requires declaration and a register of significant beneficial owners, and empowers the company and the Tribunal to act on non-disclosure.
content.study: A significant beneficial owner is an individual who, alone or with others, holds a prescribed beneficial interest or right, including through shares, voting rights, dividend rights or significant influence or control, as the rules define. The individual must declare the interest; the company maintains a register and files a return. The company must give notice to a person it believes to be a significant beneficial owner. Non-response can lead to application to the Tribunal for restrictions on transfer, suspension of rights, or other directions. Later amendments increased the enforcement teeth of the section, including action against the company for failure to take steps. The threshold and forms are in the Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules and must be read with the section.

examples.title: Layered holding
examples.body: An individual controlling a chain that holds the shares can be the significant beneficial owner even if not the registered member.

examples.title: Rights freeze
examples.body: Failure to declare can support a Tribunal order restricting transfer and voting.

distinctions: Section 89 is the declaration of beneficial interest by the registered holder and the beneficial owner. Section 90 is the significant beneficial owner regime aimed at the natural person.

misconceptions.correction: Section 90 requires declaration and a register of significant beneficial owners, and empowers the company and the Tribunal to act on non-disclosure.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is the registered body corporate the significant beneficial owner?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The regime looks through to the individual. A body corporate is not itself the significant beneficial owner.
